en.p: As shown in the figure, $\mathrm{ABC}$ is a right triangle with $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}=3$, $\overline{\mathrm{BC}}=4$, and $\angle \mathrm{B}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Let $\mathrm{D}$ be the point that internally divides segment $\mathrm{AB}$ in the ratio $2:1$.

Let $\mathrm{E}$ be the point where the circle centered at $\mathrm{A}$ with radius $\overline{\mathrm{AD}}$ meets segment $\mathrm{AC}$, and let $\mathrm{F}$ be the point, other than $\mathrm{D}$, where line $\mathrm{AB}$ meets this circle. Point $\mathrm{G}$ is chosen on arc $\mathrm{EF}$ so that $\overline{\mathrm{CG}}=2\sqrt{6}$.

Point $\mathrm{H}$ lies on the circle passing through the three points $\mathrm{C}$, $\mathrm{E}$, $\mathrm{G}$ and satisfies $\angle \mathrm{HCG}=\angle \mathrm{BAC}$. What is the length of segment $\mathrm{GH}$? [4 points]
